Section 2: Current Service Delivery and Referral Practices
Are there any Community Pharmaceutical Premises (CPPs), including ADDOs and pharmacies, operating within this health facility's catchment area?
Does this health facility currently receive clients referred from Community Pharmaceutical Premises (CPPs), including ADDOs and pharmacies?
How frequently does this health facility document referral outcomes for clients referred from CPPs?
What are the main reasons clients are referred from CPPs to this health facility? (Select all that apply)
Other — please specify
During the last 30 days, how many clients referred from CPPs received the intended services at this health facility?
Number of referred clients who received the intended services
What methods are currently used by CPPs to refer clients to this health facility? (Select all that apply)
Other — please specify
How frequently does this health facility provide feedback to CPPs regarding referred clients?
What methods does this health facility use to provide referral feedback to CPPs? (Select all that apply)
Other — please specify
Does this health facility currently coordinate with Community Health Workers (CHWs) regarding follow-up of clients referred from CPPs?
What are the main challenges experienced when receiving and managing referrals from CPPs? (Select all that apply)

valueCoding.display: Poor communication between CPPs and health facilities

Section 3: Coordination among the Healthcare Providers
Do you know the Community Health Workers from your catchment area?
Do you know the number of CPPs in your catchment area?
Do CPP dispensers and Community Health Workers (CHWs) currently collaborate with health facilities in providing healthcare services?
What forms of collaboration currently exist between the CHWs and these health facilities? (Select all that apply)

valueCoding.display: Sharing information on clients requiring healthcare services
Coordinating client referrals to health facilities
Coordinating with CHWs within the catchment area to facilitate further follow-up of referred clients who have already received services
Reporting CHW service delivery activities to the respective health facility for supervision and performance monitoring
Conducting joint weekly or monthly meetings between CHWs and health facility staff to review progress, discuss challenges, and agree on improvement actions

item.text: Other — please specify
What forms of coordination currently exist between CPPs and health facilities? (Select all that apply)

valueCoding.display: Referring clients to health facilities for further assessment and management
Receiving clients referred from health facilities with prescriptions for medicine dispensing
Receiving feedback from health facilities on clients referred by the CPP
Sharing information with health facilities on client referrals and services provided
Participating in joint meetings or discussions with health facility staff to improve service coordination

item.text: Other — please specify
What are the main challenges affecting coordination between CPPs, CHWs, and health facilities? (Select all that apply)

valueCoding.display: Lack of awareness of CHWs operating within the CPP's catchment area
Lack of awareness among CHWs and health facility staff of CPPs operating within their catchment area
Delayed or lack of feedback on referred clients
Limited sharing of client and service-related information
Lack of clear referral procedures and guidelines
Limited mechanisms for coordination among CPPs, CHWs, and health facilities

Section 5: Organizational Readiness for Afya-Tek
Give an introduction to Afya-Tek before asking these questions. Rate each statement: 1 = Strongly disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly agree, 6 = I don't know.
This health facility is ready to receive and manage digital referrals from Community Pharmaceutical Premises (CPPs).
Healthcare workers are willing to collaborate with CPPs from your catchment area.
Digital referrals from Community Pharmaceutical Premises (CPPs) can be integrated into the routine systems of this health facility.
This health facility has adequate management support to implement digital referral services from the UCS–CPP platform.
Healthcare workers at this facility would require additional training to effectively manage digital referrals from the UCS–CPP platform.
Existing referral procedures at this health facility can accommodate referrals received through the UCS–CPP platform.
This health facility has designated personnel responsible for receiving and managing client referrals.
Section 6: Perceived Usefulness and Acceptability
Rate each statement: 1 = Strongly disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly agree, 6 = I don't know.
The UCS–CPP platform could improve referral coordination between CPPs and health facilities.
The UCS–CPP platform could improve continuity of care for clients referred from CPPs.
The UCS–CPP platform could improve communication between CPP providers and healthcare workers.
The UCS–CPP platform could reduce delays in receiving and managing client referrals.
The UCS–CPP platform could improve the quality of healthcare services provided to referred clients.
I would be willing to use the UCS–CPP platform to receive and manage client referrals.
Section 7: Implementation Barriers
Rate each statement: 1 = Strongly disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly agree, 6 = I don't know.
Inadequate healthcare workers may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
High workload may limit the implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Limited digital skills among healthcare workers may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Inadequate access to smartphones, tablets, or computers may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Poor internet connectivity may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Unreliable electricity supply may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Inadequate training may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
Resistance to change among healthcare workers may hinder implementation of the Afya-Tek model.
